card.name: Highland Fling
card.tagline: The Highlands of Scotland — danced on a warrior's shield. The tight footwork is because the shield was that small.
card.profile: The Highlands of Scotland — competitive solo dance traditionally performed on the shield of a fallen enemy. The tight footwork developed because the shield was that small. Performed at every Royal Edinburgh Military Tattoo since 1950; competitive Highland dance is a Commonwealth Games invitational sport.
card.insight: The Scottish Highland Fling was traditionally danced atop a small round shield called a targe — points of the targe's central spike were intended to discipline the dancer's footwork; the modern competitive Fling has been governed by the Scottish Official Board of Highland Dancing since 1950.
